macro.ust_10y_provisional_basis: Treasury par curve; FRED H.15 pending
macro.ust_curve_basis: Treasury par curve closes (from 20 Oct; mid-session readings before)

US.why: Held. Stocks rose for a third session on 21 Oct: the S&P gained 0.58% to 7757.17, the Nasdaq 1.05% as SpaceX and Tesla led, and the Dow 0.69%. The data ran hot - producer prices up 1.3% in September, retail sales 0.8% - but the hike moved out: FedWatch had October at 16% on 22 Oct, and the 10-year closed at 5.12% on 20 Oct. The consumer is the weak point, Michigan sentiment at 46.3. The anchor holds at 6.5 on two structural points: the US is a net energy EXPORTER, a relative tailwind with Brent +75.8% y/y, and NDX at 22.4x forward on its last verified reading sat below its 10y and 5y averages. J.P. Morgan's 2027 assumptions lift US large caps to 7.5% from 6.7%; that is already in every US fund's base return, so it does not move the anchor as well.
US.summary: Held: the S&P rose 0.58% to 7757.17, a third straight gain; October hike odds are 16%, and the anchor holds.

EUROPE.why: Held, 3M at 2.25. Eurostat confirmed September inflation at 3.8% on 16 Oct, unchanged from the flash and up from 3.2%, with energy at 18.8% and core at 2.5% - the outcome that tests, at the 29 Oct meeting, the ECB's word that its cycle ended at 2.50% on 10 Sep. The 10-year OAT-Bund spread eased to 135.5bp on 14 Oct from about 140bp as the Assembly took up a budget meant to cut the deficit to 5.0% of GDP from 5.4%. The policy/growth mismatch stands against IMF growth of 0.9%. Europe is the largest net energy importer here, facing Brent +75.8% y/y. 6M and longer held. The offset is real - at 15.4x forward it is the cheapest large market after Asia.
EUROPE.summary: Held: euro-area inflation was confirmed at 3.8%, putting the ECB's 29 Oct decision to the test.

ASIA.why: Near horizons held; the ten-year anchor at 7.0 since 21 Oct. The selling returned on 22 Oct: the KOSPI fell 3.52% to 5,533.77 as the Bank of Korea paused at 3.00% and chipmakers sold - SK Hynix 5.48%, Samsung Electronics 4.02% - back below its 5552.74 close of 20 Oct and 21.0% below its 7003.74 close of 2 Oct; the Nikkei fell 2.65% to 62,907.84. China grew 4.5% in the third quarter against 4.4% expected, on exports. The earnings did not break: TSMC's third-quarter profit rose 68.7% to a record, and Samsung's quarter was a record 107.4tn won. Oil is the importers' problem, Brent at $108.82, with the yen near 158.48. The anchor was cut because half its case was the base return: it cited J.P. Morgan's EM equity assumption as the highest of any equity block, but that assumption is the Asia fund's base, so it was counted twice - and the 2027 edition cuts it to 7.1% from 7.8%, below US large caps. What remains is valuation: 10.5x forward before the fall against consensus EPS growth of ~52% and ~28% is a two-decade-wide discount.
ASIA.summary: Near horizons held: the KOSPI fell 3.52% on 22 Oct as the Bank of Korea paused, 21.0% below 2 Oct.

PHILIPPINES.why: Near horizons held. BSP raised its policy rate 50bp to 5.50% on 22 Oct, twice the 25bp that 20 of 22 analysts expected - its fourth straight hike and the first half-point since February 2023. The peso printed a record 63.545 intraday that day; its close is not carried until the official figure is reached, so the record close stays 63.361 of 21 Oct, a 7.21% loss of purchasing power against the dollar this year. The PSEi fell 0.72% to 5779.73, ending a five-session rally, still clear of its 5610.39 low of 8 Oct. September inflation was 7.2%, core 4.7%. The carry is rising to meet it: the 19 Oct auction lifted 91-day bills to 5.992% and 364-day bills to 6.444%, a ninth straight weekly rise, before the hike; 26 Oct is the first auction after it. Against 7.2% every tenor's real yield is still below zero. The 12-month and ten-year horizons stay neutral: a BSP that hikes restores the real carry. This sleeve's job - zero duration risk and high nominal carry - is unimpaired. Its purchasing power is not.
PHILIPPINES.summary: Near horizons held: BSP hiked 50bp to 5.50% on 22 Oct; the PSEi fell 0.72% and the peso printed a record 63.545 intraday.

drivers.name: Monetary policy & liquidity
drivers.note: HELD at 2.0. Manila tightened harder than priced: on 22 Oct BSP raised its policy rate 50bp to 5.50%, a fourth straight hike and the first half-point since February 2023, where 20 of 22 analysts had expected 25bp; the overnight corridor is 5.00-6.00%. Governor Remolona said the hike answered inflation, not the peso, and left 17 Dec open. The Fed pricing has barely moved: CME FedWatch had an October hike at 16% on 22 Oct, against 14.9% on 16 Oct and 31.6% after the CPI, and one by December at 90%, from 88.9%. The long end is flat: on official closes the 10-year was 5.09% on the 16th, 5.15% on the 19th and 5.12% on the 20th, with the 2-year at 4.79% and the 30-year at 5.42%; market quotes put the 21st near 5.13%, not carried until the par curve publishes. That is below the 7 Oct intraday high of 5.365%, which is above the 5 Oct peak of 5.349% and the highest since April 2002. The Bank of Korea paused at 3.00% on 22 Oct; the FOMC decides on 28 Oct, the ECB on 29 Oct and the BoJ, at 1.25%, on 30 Oct. Held: a December Fed hike is still nine-in-ten priced, and BSP's extra 25bp tightens the peso economy while lifting the money market's carry.
drivers.summary: Held: BSP hiked 50bp to 5.50% on 22 Oct against 25bp expected; FedWatch had December at 90%.

drivers.name: Inflation trajectory
drivers.note: HELD at 2.0; no new US price data. The pipeline print stands: producer prices rose 1.3% in September, the largest monthly rise since March 2022, and 6.3% on the year, with core at 0.5% and 5.0%, after CPI of 3.7% (core 2.6%). Oil is holding near its highs: Brent settled at $108.82 on 21 Oct, up 3 cents, after a $111.99 session high on the 20th, against $61.91 a year earlier - Brent +75.8% y/y - and rose about 1.7% in Asian trading on the 22nd as the US ordered diplomats out of Saudi Arabia; December WTI, the front month since November expired at $101.79 on the 20th, settled at $97.15, down 0.68%. The euro area confirmed 3.8% for September, core 2.5%; the Philippines is at 7.2%, which BSP met with a 50bp hike. Held: US core CPI at 2.6% is still contained, and the producer jump is energy passing through, not yet wages.
drivers.summary: Held: no new US price data after September's 1.3% producer-price jump; Brent settled at $108.82, +75.8% y/y.

drivers.name: Growth momentum
drivers.note: HELD at 4.0. China beat by a little: third-quarter GDP grew 4.5% on the year against 4.4% expected, up from 4.3%, but exports did the work - September retail sales rose only 1.1%. US September retail sales rose 0.8% against 0.3% expected, though gasoline did much of it: sales excluding gas stations rose only 0.2%. Michigan sentiment, at 46.3 in October's first read, is near May's record low of 44.8; ISM services (54.9) and manufacturing (54.5) stayed in expansion in September. Philippine growth was 2.6% in the first half. Held: China's beat is export-led, and a record-low US consumer is a warning, not a break.
drivers.summary: Held: China's third-quarter GDP grew 4.5% against 4.4% expected, on exports; US retail sales rose 0.8%, mostly gasoline.

drivers.name: Corporate earnings
drivers.note: HELD at 7.0, still the strongest pillar; the market is pricing the financing, not the profits. TSMC's third-quarter net income was NT$763.06bn, +68.7% on a year earlier and above the NT$746.34bn expected; Samsung's preliminary quarter was a record 107.4tn won. Asia ex-Japan EPS of ~+52% (2026) and ~+28% (2027) stands. US results carried the index again on 21 Oct: the S&P rose 0.58% to 7757.17 and the Nasdaq 1.05% as SpaceX and Tesla led. Asia's chip selling returned on the 22nd - the KOSPI fell 3.52%, SK Hynix 5.48% and Samsung Electronics 4.02%, a day after a 3.29% rebound. Held: the numbers keep beating; the multiple paid for them and the cost of funding the build-out are what move.
drivers.summary: Held, the strongest pillar: US results lifted the S&P 0.58% on 21 Oct; the KOSPI fell 3.52% as chips sold.

drivers.name: Valuation support
drivers.note: HELD at 8.0. The S&P closed at 7757.17 on 21 Oct, below its 7818.93 record of 6 Oct. Asia was on 10.5x forward before its October fall and is cheaper on the same earnings, the KOSPI 21.0% below its 2 Oct close after Thursday's fall; NDX at 22.4x forward on its last verified reading sat below its 10y (22.9x) and 5y (24.7x) averages; Europe is at 15.4x. Held, not raised: no multiple has been re-verified since the sell-off.
drivers.summary: Held: the S&P closed at 7757.17, below its 7818.93 record; the KOSPI is 21.0% below its 2 Oct close.

drivers.name: Volatility & risk appetite
drivers.note: HELD at 2.75. The VIX fell again, 3.64% to 16.68 on 21 Oct, a third close below the long-run 19.5; but Asia sold off the next day - the KOSPI fell 3.52% and the Nikkei 2.65% on 22 Oct - and the Gulf escalated. The October future settled on the 21st and no full strip for that day has been reached, so the curve stays quoted at the 20 Oct settlements - November 18.49 and December 18.7, above spot, the ordinary upward slope - and mean-reverts to the long run beyond. Tested against that day's VIX3M of 18.99 it gives 18.29 at three months, 3.66% below, inside the 10% bound; the 5 Oct strip it replaced read 4.66% below on the same test. Blended, the curve sits at 19.05, 0.45 below the long run. Held, not raised: calm on the S&P, not in Asia or the Gulf.
drivers.summary: Held: the VIX fell 3.64% to 16.68, a third close below the long run, but Asia sold off on the 22nd.

drivers.name: Geopolitics & energy
drivers.note: HELD at 1.5, with the escalation now on land. On 22 Oct the US ordered non-emergency diplomats and their families out of Saudi Arabia after Houthi strikes: an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one and injured eight, and a drone on an Aramco-run field killed two. The New York Times reports US and Israeli plans for renewed strikes on Iran after the 3 November midterms; indirect talks continue. On 21 Oct Iran's speaker Ghalibaf said Tehran would not trust Washington until its conditions for reopening the Strait were met, and CENTCOM called Iran's claims that mines had hit tankers false. Brent settled at $108.82 on 21 Oct and rose about 1.7% in Asian trading on the 22nd. Read it on VOLUME, the measure this note goes by: Kpler had oil through Hormuz, with Gulf of Oman transfers, at about 14 mb/d in the week to 18 Oct, 82% of pre-war on preliminary figures, and the Gulf's exports by every route above 24 mb/d against 23.3 pre-war; the week to 14 Oct read 9.4 mb/d on a crude-only basis, so the two are not a trend. On 22 Sep Saudi Arabia restarted the 1200 km East-West pipeline that bypasses the Strait. Vessel counts disagree and are not supply: IMF PortWatch counted 4 transits on 18 Oct against an 85 baseline, a 95% drop; Lloyd's List Intelligence 14 a day in the week to 23 Aug, counting only cargo over 10000 dwt; the US government around 30, on a basis it does not state. Held, not cut: the barrels are moving, and 1.0 is kept for full closure with Brent above $130 - strictly worse, and nearer than it was.
drivers.summary: Held: the US ordered diplomats out of Saudi Arabia on 22 Oct after Houthi strikes; Hormuz flows were near 14 mb/d, 82% of pre-war.

funds.target: Own mandate: outperform PH bank deposits, average portfolio duration <= 1 year
funds.fee_note: 0.57% trustee + 0.01% other as a share of average daily NAV (KIIDS; the listed trust fee is 0.50% p.a.), was 0.71% on a superseded KIIDS
funds.gross_note: 10y average PH short-rate path. Anchored on the PH bill curve - 91d 5.992%, 182d 6.229%, 364d 6.444% at the 19 Oct auction, higher across the curve than when this assumption was set on 2 Sep - with BSP at 5.50% after a fourth consecutive hike (a half-point on 22 Oct), reverting toward a ~4.50% neutral policy rate by year 3-5. Held at 4.85% and flagged rather than re-fitted: the rise sits in the part of the path that reverts within a few years, which lifts a ten-year average by roughly a tenth of a point, a little more after the half-point - inside this assumption's precision, but a known upward bias until it is re-fitted. CUT from 5.25% when the mandate lengthened to 10 years: the elevated front end is a 1-3 year feature, so over a decade far more of the path sits at neutral and the average falls toward it.
funds.dd_k_why: Not applicable - the cash sleeve is floored by a rate shock, not by the equity formula.

catalysts.why: The first after BSP's 50bp hike to 5.50% on 22 Oct; the 19 Oct auction had 91-day bills at 5.992%. The money market's carry reprices from here, and against 7.2% inflation the real yield is what to watch.
FedWatch had a hike at 16% for October and 90% by December on 22 Oct: a pause now and a hike in December is the priced path.
At 2.50% after the 10 Sep hike, with September inflation confirmed at 3.8%; another hike would say the energy shock outweighs growth of 0.9%.
At 1.25% after the 18 Sep hike. Most expect a hold now and a move by December; the yen is near 158.48 per dollar.

The date both sides of the Hormuz talks work to: the US pledged on 8 Oct not to strike Iran before it, and on 22 Oct the New York Times reported US and Israeli strike plans for after it. Full closure, the stress table's worst row, is the state this date can bring back.

dd_model.note: 1.65 is the calibration anchor, not the coefficient every sleeve uses. Each fund carries a declared adjustment for the shape of its own left tail; the portfolio coefficient is the weighted average across the equity sleeves. The whole quantity is then scaled by sqrt(horizon / calibration window), because expected maximum drawdown grows with the square root of the horizon - the -20% and -33% anchors are rolling FIVE-year medians and cannot simply be relabelled for a longer mandate.

scenarios.desc: Already partly running since the late-August tanker strikes. This row models the tail: full Strait closure and Brent to $130+ from $109. Global CPI re-accelerates, the Fed is forced to hike, and multiples compress hardest at the long end.

scenarios.desc: A second hike on top of the one the dot plot already has (median 4.1% for end-2026) - 4 of 18 participants see it. The Fed hikes into a 4.2% unemployment rate; duration-heavy growth de-rates.

scenarios.name: AI capex digestion

scenarios.name: Disinflation restart
